note: Freeze candidate for coding construct only. Seeds are not study-grade until freeze review PASS + calibration suite PASS.

EDIT_THRASH.definition: Repeated low-yield edit or rewrite cycles that consume trajectory steps without durable progress toward the objective oracle.
inclusion: >=3 edit-like tool spans in a short window with oscillating or reverting content
edit retries on the same locus without net oracle-relevant change
churn indicators (match-count thrash, undo/redo-like rewrite loops) dominate the failing segment
exclusion: single corrective edit that then converges
many edits that are each on distinct required targets and monotonically progress
budget exhaustion alone without edit churn pattern
EDIT_THRASH.counterexample: Two targeted edits that fix distinct failing assertions and then terminal PASS path would have continued — not thrash.
requiredEvidence: ordered edit/tool spans with path or locus identifiers
indication of non-progress (revert, oscillation, repeated failed match)

INCORRECT_FILE_TARGETING.definition: Material tool activity is aimed at files or regions outside the task's required writable/semantic target set, and this mis-targeting is central to the Layer-1 failure segment.
inclusion: edits or writes outside expected writable scope for the task
probes/edits concentrated on distractor paths while required targets remain untouched
oracle-relevant files never receive the necessary change while off-target files do
exclusion: read-only exploration of off-target files without writes
on-target edits that are merely wrong content (prefer OBJECTIVE_MISS or INSUFFICIENT_CONVERGENCE)
scope ambiguity where expected writable set is itself UNKNOWN
INCORRECT_FILE_TARGETING.counterexample: Agent reads distractors then correctly edits the required file but fails oracle due to logic error — targeting OK; code OBJECTIVE_MISS or INSUFFICIENT_CONVERGENCE.
requiredEvidence: absence or insufficiency of on-target necessary edits

INSUFFICIENT_CONVERGENCE.definition: Trajectory shows partial, directionally relevant progress but never reaches an oracle-satisfying state before terminal/fail disposition.
inclusion: on-target partial fixes that leave residual oracle failures
monotonic but incomplete progress without thrash signature
stops short while remaining work is still identifiable from runtime-visible task state
exclusion: premature terminal-complete while objective unmet (prefer PREMATURE_COMPLETION)
INSUFFICIENT_CONVERGENCE.counterexample: Zero successful on-target edits and oracle still at baseline — not convergence failure; OBJECTIVE_MISS.
requiredEvidence: residual failing oracle checks at end

PREMATURE_COMPLETION.definition: Agent signals or reaches a completion-like terminal disposition while objective oracle remains unmet, without a dominant competing process pathology explaining the stop.
inclusion: terminationStatus suggests complete/success path while objectiveOracleStatus is FAIL
explicit done/complete style action while required checks still fail
stops after superficial pass markers without addressing failing oracle
exclusion: TERMINAL_FAILED / BLOCKED / BUDGET_EXHAUSTED as honest non-completion
completion after thrash where thrash is the primary story (prefer EDIT_THRASH as primary)
completion with UNKNOWN oracle (use UNKNOWN mechanism if oracle unavailable)
PREMATURE_COMPLETION.counterexample: BUDGET_EXHAUSTED with unmet oracle — budget axis PRESENT; primary mechanism may be INSUFFICIENT_CONVERGENCE or OBJECTIVE_MISS, not PREMATURE_COMPLETION.
requiredEvidence: temporal order: completion act before/without oracle satisfaction

OBJECTIVE_MISS.definition: Layer-1 FAIL is primarily a pure task/oracle miss: required outcome not achieved, without a dominant edit-thrash, mis-targeting, premature-completion, or partial-convergence signature.
inclusion: oracle FAIL with sparse or absent process pathology
wrong final content on the correct target without thrash/mis-target/premature-complete pattern
task attempted on-target but solution is simply incorrect
exclusion: clear thrash / mis-targeting / premature completion / partial convergence primary
insufficient evidence to distinguish among seeds (use UNKNOWN)
OBJECTIVE_MISS.counterexample: On-target file never touched; only distractor edits — INCORRECT_FILE_TARGETING, not OBJECTIVE_MISS.
requiredEvidence: documentation that competing seed inclusion criteria are not met

OTHER.definition: A coherent Layer-1 failure mechanism that fits none of the seed codes after inclusion/exclusion checks.
OTHER.trigger: Coder asserts none of EDIT_THRASH|INCORRECT_FILE_TARGETING|INSUFFICIENT_CONVERGENCE|PREMATURE_COMPLETION|OBJECTIVE_MISS inclusion sets are satisfied, yet a positive mechanism narrative exists.
OTHER.forbidden: Using OTHER to avoid UNKNOWN when evidence is merely insufficient.

UNKNOWN.definition: Evidence is insufficient under codebook rules to assign a positive mechanism code.
triggerAnyOf: requiredEvidence for every candidate seed missing
oracle or trajectory fields required for adjudication unavailable
coders disagree and referee rule resolves to UNKNOWN
fail-closed default when validation of a coding record fails
UNKNOWN.forbidden: Using UNKNOWN when a seed's inclusion is clearly met to soften claims.

MULTI_MECHANISM.definition: Two or more distinct seed mechanisms are supported by the run evidence, or a valid dual-coder seed-versus-OTHER disagreement prevents a single primary without violating the frozen rules.
MULTI_MECHANISM.trigger: >=2 distinct seed codes appear in supporting event votes, dual-coder primaries, or explicit competingSeedCodes; a seed-versus-OTHER dual disagreement also requires non-empty OTHER rationale. Frozen policy never uses priorityTableSeed to force a unique winner.
requiredEvidence: at least 2 distinct supporting seed codes OR a valid dual seed-versus-OTHER disagreement
MULTI_MECHANISM.forbidden: Collapsing MULTI_MECHANISM into a preferred seed because it would make R0 interesting.

confounderAxes.orthogonalityRule: Confounder axes are NOT mechanism codes. Any axis may be PRESENT alongside any mechanism code. Axes must be scored independently.

axes.MODEL_LIMITATION: Failure plausible from model competence alone given task difficulty.
axes.TOOL_FAILURE: Tool error observed in trajectory (distinct from Layer-3 linkage completeness).
axes.BUDGET_EXPOSURE: Budget exhaustion or hard call-cap binding present.
axes.CONTEXT_STATE_FAILURE: Failure tied to missing/wrong/stale context state that was or could be runtime-visible.

confounderAxes.forbiddenMapping: Do not encode Layer-3 linkage incompleteness as TOOL_FAILURE or as a mechanism code.

eventLevel.purpose: Local mechanism evidence spans; may support multiple codes across a run.

runLevel.purpose: Single primary mechanism attribution for a Layer-1 FAIL run, with optional secondaries.

rules: Only events with supportsRunPrimary=true may vote for run primary.
If zero supporting seed events → keep run-level primary if OTHER, else UNKNOWN when fallback is not a seed.
If supporting events unanimously share one seed code → that seed is primary.
If supporting events contain >=2 distinct seed codes → primary=MULTI_MECHANISM (no unique-winner shortcut).
OTHER requires run-level rationale fields; cannot be promoted from events alone without run rationale.
Event codes never auto-set runtimeActionable; actionability is adjudicated separately.
When dualCoding is supplied to the main adjudicator, refereeDualCoding overrides primary after event promotion.
A seed-versus-OTHER dual disagreement requires non-empty OTHER rationale; otherwise referee output is UNKNOWN.
promotionRules.priorityTableNote: Frozen policy: any >=2 distinct supporting seed codes ⇒ MULTI_MECHANISM. priorityTableSeed does NOT select a unique winner among competing seeds.

referee.integrationNote: adjudicateMechanismCoding(coding, dual?) applies refereeDualCoding when dual is provided; referee primary overrides event-promoted primary. A mixed seed/OTHER pair is MULTI only when the OTHER coder supplies rationale.
order: If either coder yields UNKNOWN for insufficient evidence → UNKNOWN
If primaries differ and both are seed codes → MULTI_MECHANISM
If one seed and one OTHER → MULTI_MECHANISM unless OTHER lacks required rationale (then fail-closed UNKNOWN)
Never break ties by R0 interest, narrative preference, or historical pointLabel

clauses.requirement: mechanism has an observable runtime state
Runtime can intervene on that state
intervention occurs before semantic failure becomes irreversible
mechanism attribution does not depend on ground truth unavailable at runtime

RUNTIME_VISIBLE.meaning: State/features available to Runtime at decision time

RUNTIME_DERIVABLE.meaning: Deterministically computable from runtime-visible state without sealed labels

SEALED_OFFLINE_ONLY.meaning: Requires sealed oracle/human labels unavailable online; OK for offline mechanism attribution only

POST_HOC_NARRATIVE.meaning: Story fit after the fact; invalid for actionability and weak for mechanism attribution

runtimeActionable.failClosed: Any missing clause field or SEALED_OFFLINE_ONLY/POST_HOC_NARRATIVE under C4 → runtimeActionable=false
